audit_findings.title: Receivables sales may make financing proceeds look like recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Sold-but-uncollected receivables increased $136.691m in 2025: EMEA increased $39.348m and factoring increased $97.343m; combined increase equals 43.0% of the $317.9m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Expansion of receivables sales accelerates cash reported in operating activities and can inflate cash-based OE and every projected year derived from the anchor
audit_findings.evidence: Receivables sold to unaffiliated financial institutions under the program are excluded from “Accounts receivable, net” on the company’s consolidated balance sheets and cash receipts are reflected as cash provided by operating activities on the consolidated statements of cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The financing expansion is demonstrated, but its inclusion in the stated OE is unresolved without the adjustment ledger. If retained, its size relative to the anchor is plainly capable of materially reducing estimated value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 2025 OE calculation to the $136.691m increase in sold-but-uncollected receivables and rerun all scenarios after neutralizing any included expansion proceeds while retaining financing fees.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a one-time $99 million investment-sale gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $99.0m pretax gain, equal to 31.1% of the $317.9m anchor; after-tax OE and valuation effects unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An unremoved nonrecurring gain would inflate anchor OE and all forecast and terminal cash flows; adding sale proceeds through cash could also count the same value twice
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, the company sold an investment in certain equity securities for $ 100.0 million and recorded a gain on investments of $ 99.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The gain is demonstrated, but its removal from OE is not. Its scale is large enough to materially change the modeled value if retained, even though the cash-flow statement separately classifies the $100.0m proceeds as investing cash flow.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the complete 2025 OE adjustment ledger, isolate the gain's tax effect, confirm its removal, trace the $100.0m proceeds into the latest cash balance, and rerun if either earnings or proceeds are double-counted.

audit_findings.title: Underperforming non-cancellable ECS contracts could impose losses beyond those in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $48.3m of losses filed for the first six months of 2026, including $26.6m in the second quarter, versus $18.3m for all of 2025; remaining loss unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Post-anchor contract losses reduce future OE and may require a separate provision or obligation adjustment if unavoidable losses are not captured in forecast cash flows
audit_findings.evidence: Due to the early stages and expected variability in the margins related to these contracts, the long-term performance of the agreements cannot be reasonably estimated at this time, and the company is anticipating there could be additional losses in the coming quarters on certain agreements.
audit_findings.explanation: Losses beyond the anchor are now demonstrated, not merely possible: the first-half 2026 amount equals 15.2% of the 2025 anchor and already exceeds the full-year 2025 loss. One underperforming contract will not terminate until the first quarter of 2027, while the remaining exposure cannot be estimated from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain contract-level purchase commitments, expected sales and margins, termination payments, prepaid balances, and provisions; incorporate the filed 2026 losses and rerun using only the estimated net unavoidable future loss.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to treat all cash as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum bridge exposure $244.631m, or $4.64 per share and 5.2% of the $89.42 base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any minimum operating, restricted, or tax-burdened cash should be excluded from the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: The company requires cash or committed liquidity facilities for general corporate purposes, such as funding its ongoing working capital, acquisitions, capital expenditure needs, refinancing, returning capital to shareholders, and implementing the Operating Expense Efficiency Plan.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not establish how much cash is surplus. Nevertheless, even excluding the entire balance would reduce base value only to approximately $84.78 per share, still far below the $215.97 market price, so this issue cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Document minimum operating cash, entity restrictions, offshore transfer taxes, and committed near-term uses; revise the bridge only for the portion shown not to be distributable.

audit_findings.title: Supplier-finance obligations can distort operating working capital
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,263.089m outstanding at year-end 2025, but the 2025 balance decreased $6.583m, only 2.1% of the $317.9m anchor; approximately $1.0bn remained at July 4, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes classified within accounts payable affect operating cash flow and OE: expansion can inflate OE, while contraction or unwind can depress OE and consume cash
audit_findings.evidence: However, the company agrees to make all payments to the third-party financial institutions, and the company’s right to offset balances due from suppliers against payment obligations is restricted by the agreements for those payment obligations that have been sold by suppliers.
audit_findings.explanation: No 2025 inflation is demonstrated because the supplier-finance balance decreased from $1,269.672m to $1,263.089m; that movement was small and opposite the alleged overstatement direction. The large outstanding principal should not be deducted mechanically, although subsequent contraction warrants continued reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Separate supplier-finance changes from ordinary trade-payable changes in the 2025 and first-half 2026 OE schedules and normalize only changes shown to arise from non-durable financing terms.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum 2025 OE understatement $19.750m, computed as $137.750m filed D&A less $118.0m identified eligible D&A; adding all of it would increase base value by approximately $5.27 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic expense would be added back to OE and flow through forecast and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2016 $104.3m (65.5% of filed D&A); FY2017 $103.5m (67.4% of filed D&A); FY2019 $141.7m (74.7% of filed D&A); FY2020 $150.6m (79.7% of filed D&A); FY2021 $158.2m (81.1% of filed D&A); FY2023 $149.9m (82.8% of filed D&A); FY2024 $133.5m (81.9% of filed D&A); FY2025 $118.0m (85.6% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is conservative and cannot overstate value. Even the extreme assumption that the entire residual qualifies would raise base value only to about $94.69 per share, still far below the $215.97 market price, so the valuation conclusion would not change.
audit_findings.action: Classify the $19.750m residual from filed asset and amortization schedules; rerun only for components demonstrated to be eligible add-backs.
